sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
q: Match the caesarean incision with its description — 1) Pfannenstiel incision 2) Joel-Cohen incision 3) Classical uterine incision … A) A straight transverse skin incision higher on the abdomen with blunt dissection, less pain and less blood loss B) A curved transverse skin incision with a curved fascial cut and more dissection C) A vertical incision in the upper uterine segment, used for an anterior placenta or a very preterm lower segment
exp: Joel-Cohen and Pfannenstiel are abdominal wall choices; the classical uterine incision is reserved because it rules out a future trial of labour.

sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
q: A woman with one previous lower-segment caesarean section for fetal distress is at 39 weeks with a singleton cephalic fetus of estimated weight 3.4 kg and no other risk factors. How should she be counselled?
opts: Offer a trial of labour after caesarean, since about seven in ten women succeed and the risk of uterine rupture is low
Insist on an elective repeat caesarean, because a trial of labour is never safe after a scar
Recommend induction with prostaglandins, which improves the chance of vaginal birth
Advise a home birth, since a previous lower segment scar needs no monitoring
exp: With one previous low transverse scar the success rate is around 70-75 per cent and rupture risk under one per cent, but prostaglandins are avoided.

q: All of the following contraindicate a trial of labour after caesarean EXCEPT:
opts: A single previous low transverse incision in the lower segment
A previous classical or T-shaped uterine incision
Previous uterine rupture or full-thickness myomectomy
Placenta previa or placenta accreta spectrum in the current pregnancy
exp: One previous low transverse scar is the prerequisite for offering a trial of labour; upper segment scars and placental obstruction are contraindications.

q: Fill up: In a perimortem caesarean section the baby should be delivered within ______ minutes of maternal cardiac arrest, through a ______ abdominal incision.
exp: Delivery within four minutes improves both neonatal survival and maternal venous return, so a fast midline vertical incision is used.
